s01.setup: The ferry with the harbour's lamp oil has stalled at the dock.
s01.line: That engine has not run so well in years.
s01.lit: The oil is ashore. The harbour lamp catches.

o.R: Fix the ferry engine, with no one to ask for help
o.I: Read tide and wind data to find the fault, though it takes time
o.A: Make a short video for the waiting crowd, with one hour to finish
o.S: Help passengers find food, shade and news, even if you miss the repair

s02.setup: The old stone bridge has a cracked arch. Lamp-bearers must cross by midnight.
s02.line: My father laid that arch. Good to see it lit.
s02.lit: The lamp-bearers cross. The old arch glows.

o.R: Bolt on steel supports and test each joint, in the cold night wind
o.I: Measure the cracks to find why the arch failed, all night if needed
o.A: Design a new arch and model it on screen, though first ideas often fail
o.E: Lead the repair crew and take the blame if it goes wrong

s03.setup: The tower clock that tells the lane when to light lamps is wrong.
s03.line: Right on dusk, and the whole lane is ready.
s03.lit: The tower strikes dusk. Every window lights at once.

o.R: Open the tower clock and fix its gears, in a dusty, cramped space
o.I: Write a small script to log missed chimes, though bugs may eat your evening
o.A: Redesign the clock face to read clearly, though some liked the old one
o.C: Build a repair tracker that flags what is due, then keep it updated

s04.setup: Apples are ripening faster than the village can press them.
s04.line: Sweet juice, and now a lamp. A good evening's work.
s04.lit: The orchard is calm. Its lamp swings among the trees.

o.R: Fix the juice press and run it all day, with aching arms
o.I: Test apple mixes to find why one tastes best, though most will taste bad
o.S: Teach neighbours to run the press safely, though it takes patience
o.E: Start a small juice stall on the village road, and risk unsold crates

s05.setup: Fog covers the mountain pass. The signal lamp is dim.
s05.line: Nobody was left behind in my pass tonight.
s05.lit: A thin gold line cuts the fog. The way is clear.

o.R: Mend the dim signal lamp on the windy ridge, alone in the cold
o.I: Plot a safer route from weather and map data, though you may be wrong
o.S: Keep the lost travellers talking and steady, even when they are tired and cross
o.C: Run a headcount app at the pass, rechecking whenever people move

s06.setup: Your borrowed stall is empty, except for a strange old machine.
s06.line: A lit lamp is the best sign a stall can have.
s06.lit: The bazaar glows. A lamp hangs over your stall.

o.R: Repair a neighbour's broken phone at the stall, with tiny screws and bad light
o.I: Examine the old machine to learn what it does, though it may be junk
o.E: Pitch your stall to buyers, even if some walk away
o.C: Set up a stock and price list for the stall, before the doors open

s07.setup: A wide river blocks the road. Tired lamp-bearers rest on the bank.
s07.line: The river will carry your lamp's light to the sea.
s07.lit: The group is rested. The lamp's glow drifts downstream.

o.R: Lash a raft together from what you find, with wet feet and sore arms
o.A: Sketch a new boat shape for the crossing, though it may sink first
o.S: Look after the tired travellers through the night, while others plan the crossing
o.E: Run the camp meeting and push for a decision, even if some are unhappy

s08.setup: The great loom that weaves the banners is creaking. Market day is near.
s08.line: Every banner in town will glow brighter tomorrow.
s08.lit: Banners hang over the street. A lamp glows behind them.

o.R: Fix the loom's motor and belts, crawling under it for hours
o.A: Design the banner pattern and film a promo, though some will dislike it
o.S: Coach a nervous new weaver, even if progress is slow
o.C: Log cloth stock in a simple app, and recount whenever totals do not match

s09.setup: A group must reach the cliff top by evening. The rock glows.
s09.line: From up here the road looks like a string of stars.
s09.lit: The highest lamp is lit. The cliffs shine for miles.

o.R: Rope down a short stretch to test the rock, slow and tiring work
o.A: Film a short climb video for the group, redoing shots as the light shifts
o.E: Lead the climbers up the cliff, even if some grumble
o.C: Check the harnesses against the safety list first, while the others wait

s10.setup: Salt has spilled, two traders are arguing, and a crowd is growing.
s10.line: Quiet market, warm lamp. The best kind of night.
s10.lit: The market hums. Its lamp glows above the stalls.

o.R: Load the cart and fix its broken wheel, in the hot sun
o.S: Listen to each person's worry and settle the crowd, which takes a while
o.E: Settle the argument with a deal both traders accept, though neither is fully happy
o.C: Weigh the leftover salt and record each loss, with the crowd shouting nearby

s11.setup: A clear night is coming. Visitors climb the hill to watch the stars.
s11.line: The sky has been waiting for this.
s11.lit: The hill lamp lifts its light, and the sky answers.

o.I: Write a small program to chart the stars, even if it keeps crashing
o.A: Shoot night-sky photos and edit them, though most shots will be blurry
o.S: Help visitors find a good spot to look, though the hill is crowded
o.E: Start a stargazing club and get people to join, with no promise anyone will

s12.setup: The garden of sweet lamp-herbs is overgrown, and the season is turning.
s12.line: The herbs will sleep well tonight.
s12.lit: The beds breathe. The lamp smells of rain and mint.

o.I: Test the soil with a sensor and pick better seeds, though results come slowly
o.A: Model a peaceful garden in a 3D app, even if it looks plain
o.S: Teach neighbours to grow herbs at home, answering the same questions again
o.C: Make a planting calendar with reminders, and update it each week

s13.setup: Someone found an old printing press in a cellar. Everyone wants it working.
s13.line: Ink and light. They go together.
s13.lit: Paper fills the quarter. A lamp glows above the cellar door.

o.I: Work out how the old press works from faded notes, which may lead nowhere
o.A: Write the lead story and lay out the page, rewriting if it reads badly
o.E: Launch a local news page, even if few people follow it
o.C: Proofread the pages before printing, and start again if a mistake slips through

s14.setup: Travellers rest here before the next leg. Some are unwell tonight.
s14.line: Steady light. They can rest now.
s14.lit: The house is calm. A steady lamp burns in the window.

o.I: Test the water to find what makes people ill, though most tests show nothing
o.S: Sit and talk with sick travellers, though some would rather be left alone
o.E: Lead the clinic team tonight, even if someone has to wait
o.C: Sort the medicine store and update the patient register, checking label after label

s15.setup: The square for the festival is bare, and dusk is near.
s15.line: All the lamps are lit. Let the festival begin!
s15.lit: The square is ready. Its lamp glows over the stones.

o.A: Design a festival game for the square, still tweaking as the lamps arrive
o.S: Coach the junior team for the festival match, though they may lose
o.E: Manage the festival stalls, and face the stallholders if sales are slow
o.C: Build the festival schedule and keep acts on time, working out of sight

chapters.title: The Road Wakes
chapters.line: Somewhere ahead, a girl is looking for the lamplighter too.

chapters.title: Hills and Rivers
chapters.line: The road climbs and bends. Keepers remember her in different ways.

ila.3: Ila waves her ferry lantern. "I am Ila, her student. She left three nights ago and took no oil. Will you help me?"
ila.6: Ila catches up. "Everyone says she was happy. Nobody says she was lost."

meta.noteIntro: Jyo finds a scrap of the lamplighter's note:
meta.premise: The lighthouse is dark and the lamplighter is missing. Jyo, a firefly, needs you to carry the lantern.
meta.outro: The lighthouse is lit. Every lamp you lit caught. This is the light you carry.

sharpen.title: The Salt Wind
sharpen.line: You can smell the sea. A few more lamps will sharpen your road.

2.text: She stayed one night only. Then she went on.

4.text: Her lamp here is still warm. She is one night ahead.

5.text: She tried my work for a day. She was trying them all.

7.text: I know where she went. I promised not to say.

screens.text: The lighthouse door is open. The lamp is dark. A letter lies beside it.

I put this light out myself. A lamp I lit would only show my road. I took no oil, because the oil is yours to spend. I walked ahead and tried every kind of work, so you could find yours. The road was never mine. Choose yours.
She was never lost. She went ahead to make room for you. Here is your road so far.

draft.sharpenOffer: Want a sharper picture? Light up to seven more lamps. Stop whenever you like.
draft.bonusOffer: Want a puzzle break? Two short ones, just for fun.

9.text: Another lamp. She would have liked this town.

10.text: Your road is getting clearer with every lamp.

11.text: Her footprints and yours, side by side.

12.text: Each lamp makes your picture a little sharper.

13.text: Nearly there. The lighthouse keeps your light.

14.text: One more, and your road is as clear as it gets.

15.text: Every lamp is lit. The road is yours to choose.

R: Oil on your fingers, and glad of it.
Tools, wood, and a job done.
You like to fix things. Noted.
I: You look closely before you act.
Puzzles light you up. Jyo noticed.
A: A new shape, a new colour.
Your own touch on the town.
You made something that was not there.
That looks like you. Jyo glows.
S: You went to the people first.
Someone feels better because of you.
People matter to you. Jyo hums.
E: You saw a chance and took it.
C: You like things careful and steady.
You made it tidy and clear.
A plan, then a done job.
You like to keep order. Jyo approves.
mix: A little of both. That's fine.
You split your oil. Fair enough.
Two kinds of work. No wrong answer.

meta.outroSharp: The lighthouse is lit, and your road is as clear as we can make it. This is the light you carry.
